reading_sub: A marine casualty report, written the way the paper writes them

paras: At 0412 on 14 March a bulk carrier of 32,000 tonnes ran aground in the outer approach channel of a South Atlantic port. The vessel had left her berth six hours earlier and was proceeding under pilotage at eight knots when the incident occurred.

According to the report published by the flag state, her draft had been recorded as 11.4 metres on departure and the channel had been surveyed at 12.1 metres. The under-keel clearance was described by the operator as adequate under normal conditions. Conditions that night were not normal: a falling tide, combined with a strong southerly set, was later identified as the principal contributing factor.

No injuries were reported among the twenty-two crew, and no pollution was observed. The hull was breached in two forward compartments, both of which were isolated within the hour. The cargo, loaded three days earlier, was declared unaffected. The vessel was refloated on the following tide with the assistance of two harbour tugs and was escorted to an anchorage, where she was inspected before any decision on repairs was taken.

The investigation found that the passage plan had not been amended after the tidal window was revised. The bridge team had been informed of the revision by radio, but the change was never entered in the log. The recommendations issued to the operator include a review of bridge resource management and of the procedure by which navigational information is passed between the pilot and the officer of the watch.
reading.source: Alumni by Better -- marine casualty report written for this lesson in the register of the PS-ASON reading passages

choices: To warn shipowners that harbour tugs have become too expensive.
To report one grounding and identify what allowed it to happen.
To describe the normal procedure for leaving a port under pilotage.

tf: The vessel was hard-fast in the outer approach channel.
The text says she 'ran aground in the outer approach channel'. Hard-fast is what a question calls a ship that is aground.
The grounding exacted a human toll.
The text says 'No injuries were reported among the twenty-two crew'. To exact a human toll means that people were hurt or killed.
The ship was brought back into deep water with the help of towage assets.
The text says she 'was refloated on the following tide with the assistance of two harbour tugs'. Towage assets are tugs.
The operator considered the under-keel clearance insufficient.
The text says the clearance 'was described by the operator as adequate under normal conditions'. The option keeps the topic and flips the meaning.
The revised tidal window was never reflected in the passage plan.
The text says 'the passage plan had not been amended after the tidal window was revised'.

grammar_question: Every one of these sentences hides the person who acted. Where would you put the ship, the officer or the pilot in each one -- and why does a report leave them out?
grammar_rows: the standard passive: what happened matters more than who did it
past perfect passive: it had already happened before the moment described
present passive: a standing procedure, true every day
Information is passed between the pilot and the officer.
only when the agent is the point. Most report sentences drop it
The clearance was described by the operator as adequate.
an option that turns the passive into an active names somebody the text never named. Find the verb before you look for a person.
grammar_insight: A report is written in the passive because it is about the ship, not about a person. That is exactly where the trap lives: swap the passive for an active and the option quietly appoints a guilty party the text never appointed.
grammar_practice: after the tidal window was revised.
between the pilot and the officer of the watch.

quickfire.situation: The text says the ship 'ran aground'. Which would a question write instead: went adrift, became hard-fast, or was under way?
tips: Aground means touching the bottom and not moving.
Adrift means moving with no control. Under way means moving under command.

quickfire.situation: The text says 'no injuries were reported'. Say that in the register a question would use.
tips: The incident exacted no human toll.

quickfire.situation: An option says: The operator judged the clearance to be insufficient. Is that what the text says?
tips: The text says the operator described it as adequate under normal conditions.
Insufficient is the opposite. The option keeps the topic and flips the meaning.

quickfire.situation: Give the exam-register word for the place outside a port where a ship waits at anchor.
tips: The text calls it an anchorage.

quickfire.situation: The report says: The change was never entered in the log. Who entered nothing, and why does the report not tell you?
tips: The passive leaves the agent out because the report is about the ship, not about a person.
An option that names somebody is adding information the text does not carry.

quickfire.situation: In one sentence, say what the investigation found.
tips: The passage plan had not been amended after the tidal window was revised.
The bridge team knew, but the change never reached the log.

prod_sub: Two recordings, then the report in your own words

listenings.sub: A duty officer reads the morning summary. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: Good morning. This is the outer channel summary for the fourteenth of March. At four twelve this morning a bulk carrier of thirty-two thousand tonnes went aground in the outer approach channel while proceeding under pilotage at eight knots. All twenty-two crew are accounted for and no injuries have been reported. No pollution has been observed in the channel or at the anchorage. The hull was breached in two forward compartments, and both compartments were isolated within the hour. The vessel will be refloated on the following tide with the assistance of two harbour tugs and escorted to the roadstead for inspection. Until further notice the outer channel is closed to deep-draft traffic. Vessels awaiting a berth should remain at the anchorage and keep a listening watch on channel sixteen.
questions: What happened at four twelve, and what was the ship doing at the time?
A bulk carrier of thirty-two thousand tonnes went aground in the outer approach channel while proceeding under pilotage at eight knots.
What does the officer say about the crew and about pollution?
All twenty-two crew are accounted for, no injuries have been reported, and no pollution has been observed in the channel or at the anchorage.
What are other ships told to do?
The outer channel is closed to deep-draft traffic. Vessels awaiting a berth should remain at the anchorage and keep a listening watch on channel sixteen.

listenings.h: Why the Plan Was Never Amended
listenings.sub: An investigator explains the finding. Sound first -- no text.
listenings.text: People always want a single cause, and there almost never is one. The tidal window was revised at twenty-two hundred the night before. The bridge team was told by radio, and I have no doubt that they heard it, because two of them repeated the new time back. What never happened is the next step. Nobody entered the revision in the log, and nobody amended the passage plan. So when the ship left her berth six hours later, the plan on the chart table still described a tide that no longer existed. The under-keel clearance looked adequate on paper and was not adequate in the water. That is the whole finding. It is not about one careless officer. It is about a procedure that allowed a change to be spoken and never written.
questions: When was the tidal window revised, and how did the bridge team learn about it?
It was revised at twenty-two hundred the night before, and the bridge team was told by radio. Two of them repeated the new time back.
What is the step the investigator says never happened?
Nobody entered the revision in the log and nobody amended the passage plan, so the plan on the chart table still described a tide that no longer existed.
Why does he say the finding is not about one careless officer?
Because it is about a procedure that allowed a change to be spoken and never written.

She was refloated on the following tide with the assistance of two harbour tugs.

checklist: I know ten ship words well enough to read past them without stopping.
I can read a passive sentence and say what happened without inventing who did it.

I can say a technical report back in my own words.

pc_desc: The ten core words of a ship, a real marine casualty report, and the passive voice that every incident report is written in. Key words: vessel, navigation, cargo, port, crew, bridge, hull, draft, knot, nautical mile. Structure: the passive voice in incident reports.

paras: At 0412 the vessel was reported aground in the outer channel. The hull was breached in two forward compartments, both of which were isolated within the hour. No injuries were sustained.

The investigation found that the passage plan had not been amended after the tidal window was revised. The bridge team had been informed by radio, but the change was never entered in the log. Recommendations are issued to the operator, and the procedure by which navigational information is passed between the pilot and the officer of the watch will be reviewed.

quiz.q: Why does the report say the hull was breached instead of the rocks breached the hull?
opts: Because the passive sounds more polite in English.
Because the report is about the ship and its damage, not about what caused it.
Because the verb breach has no active form in the past.

quiz.q: The passage plan had not been amended after the tidal window was revised. Which of the two happened first?
opts: The tidal window was revised, and after that the plan was still not amended.
The plan was amended, and after that the tidal window was revised.
The two happened at exactly the same moment.

quiz.q: The bridge team had been informed by radio. What does that sentence tell you about who informed them?
opts: It tells you the pilot informed them.
It tells you nobody informed them.
It tells you nothing. The passive leaves the agent out, so an option that names one is adding information.

grammar_tip_title: The Passive of an Incident Report
grammar_tip_lead: Every marine casualty report is written in the passive. Reading one is a matter of finding the verb before you look for a person, because the person is usually not there at all.
pc_blanks: Hint: be plus past participle. The damage matters, not what caused it.
The passage plan had not been
after the tidal window was revised.
Hint: officially changed. One word, past participle.
Hint: the verb an official account uses instead of said.
on the following tide with the assistance of two harbour tugs.

had been recorded as 11.4 metres on departure.

pc_order_lead: The sequence of events, as the investigation established it.
pc_order: At 0412 she ran aground and the hull was breached in two forward compartments.
The tidal window was revised at 2200 and the bridge team was informed by radio.
She was refloated on the following tide and escorted to an anchorage for inspection.
The change was never entered in the log and the passage plan was not amended.
The vessel left her berth and proceeded down the outer channel under pilotage.

media.tip: listen for the passive. Every finding is stated as something that was done, never as something somebody did.

teacher.s1: Abertura (2 min): Esta e a aula 1 de um programa que tem UM objetivo: o PS-ASON de marco de 2027. NAO cumprimente de forma scriptada (REGRA 27A) -- entre direto. DECISAO DE DESENHO: TODAS as aulas deste programa sao reading-driven, sem alternar com aula de fala (REGRA 29.2 nao se aplica aqui), porque a prova e 100% leitura, sem redacao e sem speaking. Diga isso a ela em uma frase: o que treinarmos aqui e o que cai la.
teacher.s2: Diagnostico oral (5 min): Ela ja prestou 2025 e 2026. Deixe-a falar SEM interromper e anote tres coisas: (1) ela infere palavra desconhecida pelo contexto ou trava? (2) ela fala das OPCOES ou so do texto? (3) o ingles falado dela (medido 0%) sai ou nao sai? Nao corrija nada agora. Os chips sao so para destravar.
teacher.s3: A pergunta da prova (5 min): Este e o enunciado REAL da questao 19 de 2026. Peca que ela leia em voz alta e explique o que a instrucao pede. O ponto pedagogico e um so: 'NOT true' nao pede o que o texto diz, pede o que o texto NAO sustenta -- e as cinco alternativas vao estar escritas com outras palavras. Se ela ja souber disso, otimo: confirme e siga.
teacher.s4: Objetivo (2 min): Tres missoes. Diga: ten words, one voice, one trick. Nao explique nenhuma delas agora.
teacher.s5: Transicao vocab (1 min): Diga: These ten are not the hard words. They are the words the paper assumes you already have. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s6: Vocab reveal 1-4 (5 min): Leia a pista em ingles, ela arrisca a palavra, so entao revele. NAO traduza (REGRA 13 -- B2 e zero portugues na tela). CCQ para vessel: Is a fishing boat a vessel? (Yes -- any ship or large boat.) CCQ para port: Is port the city or the place where ships berth? (Both, but here the working place.) Avise que 'port' tem OUTRO sentido a bordo -- bombordo -- e que ele volta na aula 2.
teacher.s7: Vocab reveal 5-7 (5 min): Mesma dinamica. CCQ para crew: Does crew include the master? (Yes -- everyone who works on board.) CCQ para bridge: Is the bridge where the engines are? (No -- it is where the ship is commanded.) CCQ para hull: Is the hull the whole ship? (No -- the body of it, the part in the water.)
teacher.s8: Vocab reveal 8-10 (5 min): As tres mais tecnicas e as que mais caem. CCQ para draft: Is draft how deep the water is, or how deep the ship sits in it? (How deep the ship sits.) FALSO COGNATO, e o edital cobra falso cognato explicitamente: draft aqui NAO e rascunho, e calado. Peca a diferenca entre knot e nautical mile em voz alta -- knot e VELOCIDADE, nautical mile e DISTANCIA, e confundir os dois ja custou questao.
teacher.s9: Consolidate (4 min): Ela toca a palavra e depois a definicao. Exija que LEIA a definicao em voz alta antes de fechar o par. Se errar, nao de a resposta: reformule a definicao com outras palavras -- e o mesmo movimento que a prova cobra.
teacher.s10: Transicao leitura (1 min): Diga: This is not a text about ships. It is a report, and reports have a grammar of their own. O proximo slide e o de TAREFA: a pergunta ANTES do texto.
teacher.s11: Leitura (7 min): Primeira passada em silencio, 3 minutos, SEM dicionario. NAO traduza nenhuma palavra. Se ela parar numa palavra, pergunte What do you think it means, from the sentence? -- inferir pelo contexto e exatamente o que ela tera de fazer na prova. Depois peca UMA frase de resumo. O detalhe fica para o true/false.
teacher.s12: Gist (3 min): Ela escolhe e JUSTIFICA em voz alta (Why not a? Why not c?). A justificativa oral e o exercicio, nao o clique.
teacher.s13: True or False (7 min): REGRA DA CASA, e ela vale o programa inteiro: ela diz TRUE ou FALSE e DEPOIS LE EM VOZ ALTA a linha do texto que prova. So entao clique para revelar. Sem a linha, o acerto nao vale -- na prova o que separa acerto de chute e achar a evidencia. Repare que NENHUMA das cinco afirmacoes usa a palavra do texto: e o desenho da prova, e e o assunto do capitulo 5.
teacher.s14: Transicao gramatica (1 min): Diga: You just read twenty passive verbs without noticing. Let us look at them. Ela disse que estuda gramatica sozinha -- entao aqui a gramatica entra como FERRAMENTA DE LEITURA, nunca como conteudo a produzir.
teacher.s15: Grammar discovery (7 min): Leia os 4 exemplos. NAO de a regra antes. Pergunte: Who breached the hull? Who amended the plan? Espere ela perceber que o texto nao diz. So entao clique Reveal the Rule. CCQ: If the option says 'the pilot failed to amend the plan', is that in the text? (No -- the text never names who.) Esse CCQ e o ponto inteiro da aula.
teacher.s16: Practice (4 min): Ela diz a forma ORALMENTE antes de clicar. Se travar, pergunte: before, or at the same time? Nao explique de novo.
teacher.s17: Spot the error (4 min): Leia cada frase errada. Pergunte What is wrong here? e ESPERE. Ela corrige ANTES de voce clicar. Os quatro erros sao os classicos de passiva: was + past simple, participio sem -ed, 'had not amended' sem been, e concordancia was/were.
teacher.s18: Transicao equivalencia (1 min): Diga: Now the part that decides the exam. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s19: Como a prova esconde (4 min): Estes quatro pares saiam do texto que ela acabou de ler. Leia o par 1 e pergunte: which of the two is on the page? Ela vai ver que a coluna da direita nunca esta la. Diga o numero: nas duas provas que ela enviou, quase toda questao troca a palavra do texto por um sinonimo de registro mais alto.
teacher.s20: Equivalencia (5 min): Ela toca a frase de registro alto e depois o que aquilo diz em ingles simples. Insista na direcao DIFICIL depois: cubra a coluna da direita e pergunte, para cada frase simples, como a prova escreveria aquilo.
teacher.s21: Complete (5 min): Teacher-led: leia o texto em voz alta e pare em cada lacuna. Ela escolhe do banco. Se ela hesitar, releia a frase inteira -- a colocacao decide, nao a traducao.
teacher.s22: Quick fire (6 min): Uma pergunta por vez, EM VOZ ALTA, antes de mostrar as dicas. Cronometre mentalmente: a meta e responder em menos de dez segundos. Nao deixe ela ler as dicas antes de tentar.
teacher.s23: Transicao (1 min): Diga: The exam has no listening. Your career does. Two minutes each, and the words are the same ones. Passe ao proximo.
teacher.s24: Listening 1 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Ela mediu 0% de escuta: use 0.75x na primeira vez sem pedir. Toque duas vezes, SEM texto. Depois peca que ela RESUMA em ingles o que o oficial anunciou.
teacher.s25: Listening 2 (5 min): LEIA AS 3 PERGUNTAS EM VOZ ALTA COM ELA ANTES de tocar (REGRA 2.1). Este audio da a CAUSA que o relatorio escrito so insinua. No fim pergunte: which of the two -- the report or this man -- tells you more, and why?
teacher.s26: Role-play guiado (4 min): Ela conta o relatorio em cinco frases usando os frames. NAO corrija durante. Conte quantas passivas corretas ela produz e diga o numero no fim -- e o indicador concreto de progresso.
teacher.s27: Role-play semi-livre (5 min): A proibicao das tres palavras e o exercicio inteiro: forcar a parafrase e forcar o registro alto. Se ela usar uma das tres, so aponte com o dedo e espere -- nao de a alternativa.
teacher.s28: Producao livre (6 min): Nao interrompa e nao corrija durante. O que voce esta medindo e se ela consegue NOMEAR a linha de evidencia e NOMEAR a palavra substituida. Se ela conseguir nas duas, a aula 1 cumpriu o objetivo. Reformule depois, sem apontar erro.
teacher.s29: Transicao wrap-up (1 min): Diga: Let us see what you can do now that you could not do an hour ago.
teacher.s30: Survival card (3 min): Cinco frases DO PROPRIO texto. Toque o audio e peca que ela repita. A pronuncia aqui nao e enfeite: palavra que ela nunca pronunciou e palavra que ela pula quando le.
teacher.s31: Checklist (2 min): Leia cada item em voz alta. Os 5 checks marcados fecham a aula e acendem o stamp (o sistema grava sozinho no Supabase).
teacher.s32: Encerramento (2 min): Diga: Lesson 1 complete, Helena. HOMEWORK ORALMENTE, nunca escrito na tela: (1) baixar a prova do PS-ASON 2026 e ler SO os textos, sem responder nada, marcando toda palavra que ela nao entende por completo; (2) escrever, sem dicionario, uma lista de dez palavras maritimas que ela ja sabe em ingles. As duas coisas entram na aula 2 e viram a linha de base dela. Proxima aula: The Ship's World.
